Round 1 - Riddle 1: The Forged Manifest.subtitle: The Forged Manifest
Round 1 - Riddle 1: The Forged Manifest.text: A file that doesn't look quite right has been left behind. Sometimes, the first step in solving a mystery is simply asking: what exactly am I looking at?
Round 1 - Riddle 1: The Forged Manifest.hint: Don't judge a file by its extension. Let the MIME type speak.

Round 1 - Riddle 2: Follow the Trail.subtitle: Follow the Trail
Round 1 - Riddle 2: Follow the Trail.text: A familiar car wash hides more than just dirty cars. Somewhere behind the business is a lawyer, and your job is to uncover his real name and phone number using publicly available information.
Round 1 - Riddle 2: Follow the Trail.hint: Start with the car wash. Follow the trail through public records and business information. Flag Format: coredump{abc_xyz_123_456}

Round 1 - Riddle 3: Message in a Bottle.subtitle: Message in a Bottle
Round 1 - Riddle 3: Message in a Bottle.text: This image looks innocent enough... but there's more hiding inside it than what meets the eye. Dig into its metadata and investigate what the image may be concealing.
Round 1 - Riddle 3: Message in a Bottle.hint: Start by examining the image's metadata. If that doesn't reveal everything, look for something hidden within the file itself.

Round 1 - Riddle 4: Dead Man's Switch.subtitle: Dead Man's Switch
Round 1 - Riddle 4: Dead Man's Switch.text: My friend hid the flag somewhere inside a pile of complete gibberish — and then encoded the entire thing. Can you work your way through the mess and find what was hidden?
Round 1 - Riddle 4: Dead Man's Switch.hint: The gibberish isn't the only thing you need to decode. Sometimes, one layer of encoding leads to another.

Round 1 - Riddle 5: The Bovine Cipher.subtitle: The Bovine Cipher
Round 1 - Riddle 5: The Bovine Cipher.text: I asked a cow for the flag, but all it gave me was a strange sequence of moos in two different tones. Maybe the cow is trying to tell you something...
Round 1 - Riddle 5: The Bovine Cipher.hint: Two different tones. Two different symbols. Think about a code that only needs two states.

Round 1 - Riddle 6: Sailor's Compass.subtitle: Sailor's Compass
Round 1 - Riddle 6: Sailor's Compass.text: An old navigator carved this sequence onto his compass brass: YmxhY2tiZWFyZHtzYWlsb3JzX2NvbXBhc3NfcG9pbnRzX25vcnRofQ==. Can you decode where the needle points?
Round 1 - Riddle 6: Sailor's Compass.hint: Base64 is the classic merchant tongue of the digital seas.

Round 1 - Riddle 7: Ghost Signal.subtitle: Ghost Signal
Round 1 - Riddle 7: Ghost Signal.text: A phantom vessel transmitting on port 1337 keeps repeating an ICMP packet sequence. The payload carries the hex string: 6c6f7374636f64657b67686f73745f7369676e616c5f666f756e647d. Intercept and decode it.
Round 1 - Riddle 7: Ghost Signal.hint: Convert hexadecimal byte pairs into plain ASCII characters.

Round 1 - Riddle 8: The Quarterdeck.subtitle: The Quarterdeck
Round 1 - Riddle 8: The Quarterdeck.text: The quarterdeck inspection ledger has an HTML comment hidden deep inside the harbor portal markup: <!-- FLAG: lostcode{always_inspect_the_quarterdeck_source} -->. Find the hidden flag.
Round 1 - Riddle 8: The Quarterdeck.hint: Right-click and inspect the page elements or check comments in page source.

Round 1 - Riddle 9: Smuggler's Cask.subtitle: Smuggler's Cask
Round 1 - Riddle 9: Smuggler's Cask.text: A barrel marked with pirate runes has a secret string encoded in Morse code: .-.. --- ... - -.-. --- -.. . { ... -- ..- --. --. .-.. . .-. ... _ -.-. .- ... -.- }. Decipher the tapped rhythm.
Round 1 - Riddle 9: Smuggler's Cask.hint: Dots and dashes—translate each letter using a standard Morse code chart.

Round 1 - Riddle 10: Kraken's Cipher.subtitle: Kraken's Cipher
Round 1 - Riddle 10: Kraken's Cipher.text: The sea monster's curse shifted every letter forward by 13 positions (ROT13): ybfgpbqr{xenvra_fyrrcf_va_gur_qrrc}. Break the shift to calm the waters.
Round 1 - Riddle 10: Kraken's Cipher.hint: Caesar cipher with a rotation shift of 13.

Round 2 - Riddle 1: The Governor's Vault.subtitle: The Governor's Vault
Round 2 - Riddle 1: The Governor's Vault.text: We stumbled upon the new Employee Portal for CoreDump Corp. They claim their new architecture is incredibly secure and that employees can only view their own notes. See if you can prove them wrong and uncover the admin's secret.

Round 2 - Riddle 2: The Caribbean Log.subtitle: The Caribbean Log
Round 2 - Riddle 2: The Caribbean Log.text: 9 years ago, during the first quarter of the year, a traveler named Clemens visited a restaurant somewhere in the Caribbean. Before leaving, he wrote an online review describing his experience. He described the location as gorgeous and surrounded by the Caribbean Sea, but wasn't impressed with the service or the food considering the price. During his visit, Clemens also purchased a drink. Your task is to identify the restaurant he visited, find the drink he ordered, and determine how much it cost in Dominican pesos.
Round 2 - Riddle 2: The Caribbean Log.hint: Hint: Don’t focus only on the text—the information linked to the image may lead you to the answer. Flag Format : coredump{restaurantname_drinkname_priceinnumbers}

Round 2 - Riddle 3: Siren's Call.subtitle: Siren's Call
Round 2 - Riddle 3: Siren's Call.text: We intercepted a strange ping sweep on our network. It looks like normal diagnostic traffic, but our intrusion detection system flagged a weird payload signature. Can you extract the hidden data?
Round 2 - Riddle 3: Siren's Call.hint: I am always before your eyes, but you scan right past me.

Round 2 - Riddle 4: Cipher Chest.subtitle: Cipher Chest
Round 2 - Riddle 4: Cipher Chest.text: Two messages were encrypted using the exact same One-Time Pad (OTP) key. We know the plaintext of the first message is: "The weather in London is terrible today." - transmission1.hex contains the encrypted first message. - transmission2.hex contains the encrypted flag. Recover the flag from transmission2.hex.
Round 2 - Riddle 4: Cipher Chest.hint: [ Transmission 1 = Plaintext 1 ⊕ Key ] , [ Transmission 2 = Plaintext 2 ⊕ Key ]

Round 2 - Riddle 5: Port Royal Infiltrat.subtitle: Port Royal Infiltration
Round 2 - Riddle 5: Port Royal Infiltrat.text: The harbor master's login checks credentials with a fragile query: SELECT * FROM captains WHERE user = '$user' AND pass = '$pass'. Inject the payload ' OR 1=1 -- to bypass authentication and capture the harbor ledger flag: lostcode{port_royal_gates_bypassed_via_sqli}.
Round 2 - Riddle 5: Port Royal Infiltrat.hint: Classic SQL injection authentication bypass using single quotes and comments.

Round 2 - Riddle 6: Blackbeard's Logbook.subtitle: Blackbeard's Logbook
Round 2 - Riddle 6: Blackbeard's Logbook.text: A memory slice from Blackbeard's encrypted flash drive revealed an environmental variable: EXPORT SECRET_FLAG=lostcode{blackbeards_memory_dump_unsealed}. Recover the secret token.
Round 2 - Riddle 6: Blackbeard's Logbook.hint: Check environment variables and process memory strings.

Round 3 - Riddle 1: Sunken Registers.subtitle: Sunken Registers
Round 3 - Riddle 1: Sunken Registers.text: One of our highly secure production servers experienced a fatal hardware failure and crashed. We managed to extract the executable and the resulting core memory dump. We believe the secret encryption flag was loaded into memory right before the crash. Since the binary is stripped, can you dive into the memory dump and find it?
Round 3 - Riddle 1: Sunken Registers.hint: The 'strings' command won't save you here because the flag isn't stored as continuous text in memory. Load the core dump into GDB along with the executable, figure out where the data was loaded, and inspect the raw memory registers to pull out the raw hex values.

Round 3 - Riddle 2: Ghost Mechanism.subtitle: Ghost Mechanism
Round 3 - Riddle 2: Ghost Mechanism.text: Solve the Reverse Engineering challenge and submit your flag.
Round 3 - Riddle 2: Ghost Mechanism.hint: There are way too many complex equations in this binary to solve by hand or brute force. Try using an advanced solver script like the Z3 Theorem Prover, or a symbolic execution framework like Angr to find the mathematical path to success.

Round 4 - Riddle 1: Walk the Plank.subtitle: Walk the Plank
Round 4 - Riddle 1: Walk the Plank.text: We managed to get a copy of the company's secure chat portal executable. It's heavily protected by modern memory mitigations (Stack Canaries). Can you find a way to bypass the protections and access the secret admin function to reveal the flag?
Round 4 - Riddle 1: Walk the Plank.hint: The 'gets()' function gives you a classic buffer overflow, but the Stack Canary will crash the program before you can win. Notice how the program prints back your alias? Try entering format string specifiers (like %15$p) to leak the secret Canary off the stack so you can perfectly place it back during your overflow.
